library.overview: Imagine an intruder who wants to enter a high-security bank without raising an alarm. Instead of breaking down the front door in a ski mask, they hire an official armored bank truck, freeze it inside the garage before the driver even starts the route, and pocket two golden master keys: the first master key unlocks the rear cargo doors so they can empty all the legal bank gold and load their own covert crew inside, and the second master key unlocks the driver cab so they can reprogram the GPS route and release the brake. When the truck rolls out, every security camera and guard at the gate still sees the bank’s own trusted license plate and uniform. In this scenario (T1055.012, Process Hollowing & Cobalt Strike Beacon Loader) on WKS-04 (10.10.4), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: launching a Legitimate Windows Process, then hollowing Out the Original svchost.exe Code, then allocating Writable-Executable Memory, then hijacking the CPU Thread Context. Steps #1–#5 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Launching a Legitimate Windows Process, then Hollowing Out the Original svchost.exe Code, then Allocating Writable-Executable Memory, then Hijacking the CPU Thread Context, then Outbound HTTPS Command-and-Control Beacon. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

library.name: Fileless AMSI Memory Bypass & Reflective DLL Injection
library.shortSubtitle: Malware Analysis · amsi.dll 6-Byte Patch & In-Memory CLR Load
library.overview: Picture a glass-walled precision workshop that has its own automated X-Ray inspection belt built right inside the room, wired up to an elevated security watchtower overhead. Normally, whenever a red contraband canister slides onto the belt, the X-Ray scanner triggers a loud siren and slams a heavy steel drop-gate shut. Because the scanner circuit panel sits inside the exact same room as the workbench, a covert technician simply walks over, unbolts the blue glass safety hatch with a brass master wrench, pulls out all six copper inspection fuses, snaps in a single six-pin brass short-circuit jumper that cuts off the watchtower cable, and shuts the glass hatch again. Then, without ever unlocking the warehouse floor door or tipping the digital floor scale past zero kilograms, an overhead pneumatic air-tube drops floating parts onto a mid-air levitation ring where they snap together into a live hovering drone while the watchtower upstairs still reads all clear. In this scenario (T1562.001 and T1620, Fileless AMSI Memory Bypass & Reflective DLL Injection) on WKS-FIN-09, a hidden PowerShell session spawned by Microsoft Word sabotages its own in-process Antimalware Scan Interface before loading a stage-2 payload strictly in volatile RAM. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: locating the live scanner function in process memory, unlocking its read-only code page, overwriting six opening instruction bytes so every future scan returns an immediate skip result, and finally streaming a reflective assembly straight from HTTPS into unbacked RAM with zero disk writes. Steps #1-#4 walk that complete kill chain end-to-end, while Memory Forensics compares live patched pages and unbacked executable RAM against the clean disk. Primary detection correlates PowerShell Script Block Event ID 4104 with kernel memory-protection telemetry and empty-path CLR assembly load events.

library.overview: Picture a busy municipal records hall divided into two wings: on the left sits a climate-controlled safety archive with four spinning silver microfilm backup reels beside an emergency green recovery lever, and on the right stand four glass-fronted filing vaults stacked with crisp white paper ledgers. Suddenly, an armored brass dispatch capsule shoots down an overhead service chute from a remote hallway, unlocks the hall master breaker, and wakes a roaring industrial ribbon shredder. Before touching a single active ledger, the saboteur feeds all four silver backup reels straight into the shredder teeth until silver confetti fills the bin and snaps the green recovery lever clean off its hinge. Instantly, four synchronized overhead stamping arms plunge in parallel across all four filing vaults, stamping a blazing crimson lock band strictly across the top header strip of every ledger stack while leaving the lower white pages untouched, slamming four heavy cast-iron padlocks shut and bolting a giant crimson extortion notice across the glass entrance door while the ceiling audit lamp flashes bright violet. In this scenario (MITRE ATT&CK T1569.002, T1490, and T1486) targeting corporate file server FS-CORP-01 (10.10.50.14), a LockBit 3.0 affiliate executes an automated recovery-destruction and rapid head-only encryption blitz. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: remote PsExec service deployment over SMB as SYSTEM, then systematic Volume Shadow Copy deletion and boot-recovery disabling, then high-speed multi-threaded I/O Completion Port encryption of only the opening 4 KB to 64 KB of every document, then mass extortion-note placement paired with an Event Log clearing attempt. Steps #1-#4 trace each forensic artifact from System Event ID 7045 through Sysmon Event ID 1, mass .lockbit renames, and Security Event ID 1102.

library.overview: Picture a gleaming white telecommunications assembly cleanroom where sleek business desk phones glide down an aluminum conveyor toward a heavy brass authenticity press. Just before an open phone reaches the press, a dark covert robotic arm drops from an upstream supplier vent and swaps in two rigged interior pieces: a crimson-toothed brass audio gear and a frosted glass prism hiding a glowing amber wax-sealed core inside its base. Moments later, the lid snaps shut and the official factory press stamps a completely genuine gold-and-emerald hologram right onto the phone top, so the quality inspector scans the authentic seal and waves it straight onto a trader office desk. Once plugged in at the desk, the phone shell splits open in cutaway: the rigged brass gear spins first, cracks open the amber core inside the frosted prism, and unwinds a glowing ribbon into a hidden micro-radio. That radio scans an innocent framed portrait tile hanging on a public art-gallery wall, peels a secret crimson address strip off the bottom border of the frame, siphons keycards right out of the trader desk folder, and opens a private beam to an elevated high-value vault while a violet behavioral watch monitor catches a desk telephone reaching into a credential drawer. In this scenario (CVE-2023-29059, MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002, T1574.002, T1102.001, and T1555.003) documented jointly by CrowdStrike, Mandiant, and Kaspersky, Lazarus Group compromises the 3CX Windows build server via an upstream X_TRADER breach and ships a validly signed trojanized VoIP installer to WKS-TRD-14. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: pre-signing tampering of ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll, then DLL side-loading and 0xFEEDFACE RC4 decryption into unbacked RWX RAM, then GitHub IconStorages .ico steganographic C2 resolution, then ICONICSTEALER credential theft paired with selective Stage-2 Gopuram backdoor deployment. Steps #1-#4 trace the full kill chain, while Memory Forensics compares clean vs. trojanized d3dcompiler_47.dll alongside unbacked RWX implant regions.
